decision.summaryForCoordinator: FC-HOSTILE names nine DEFECTS as its input classes, so the strongest test available is whether the artifact commits any of them in its own bytes — an author illustrating an example would fail instantly. I tested all nine against the subject itself. Invalid UTF-8: strict decode of all 5027 bytes succeeds with not one non-ASCII byte. Terminal-control sequence: no byte below 0x20 but newlines, no ESC, no escapes. Path traversal: '../' zero, and the bare token '..' zero anywhere. Absolute path: no leading-slash hit and no Windows drive letter — every path is a repo-relative docs/ path. Deeply nested structure: measured depth 3. Unbounded fault string: none exists. Shell metacharacters: the only one present is the semicolon, four occurrences, each read in context — three separating the four input families inside the quoted exactByteIntent and one separating clauses in the G12 annotation; no pipe, ampersand, dollar, backtick, redirect, glob or subshell anywhere. The duplicate-key test is the one I want to flag, because the default JSON parser would have hidden it: Python resolves duplicates last-key-wins silently, so I re-parsed with an object_pairs_hook that counts keys per object. Zero duplicates. That matters beyond irony — live v4's own duplicate-key rule makes such a document a parse REFUSAL precisely because last-key-wins 'lets a document say one thing to a reader and another to every instrument while its bytes stay unchanged', and an input corpus for the hostile class carrying that defect would have BEEN that document. The PATH probe is equally clean: 'PATH' twice and both negations, with $PATH, /bin, /usr, sh -c, system(, popen, spawn and argv all at zero. The inventory reconstructs exactly at three manifest, three component, two configuration and one external-system name, nine in total, with the exactByteIntent character-for-character equal to live. Of the nine class descriptions, four are true substrings and five are derived, and the pattern is principled: v4 writes each family as a shared noun followed by a list, so each family's first member is verbatim and its continuations need the noun distributed — four families, four verbatim leads, five distributions. As in FC-DEGRADED the subject claims no verbatim status for any of them, carrying no verbatimFromV4 field at all. One thing needs your judgement. I pressed 'closed list' as a candidate SHOULD-FIX and it did not cross, but the word is the subject's, not v4's — the contract reserves 'closed' for statusTokens and the CommandResult union, so it states closure when it means it. Closure over the hostile-input SPACE would in fact be false: v4's hostileInputDiscipline premise names a lock among the attacker-influenceable inputs, yet no hostile lock is among the nine. It did not cross because both of the subject's sentences scope the word to the enumeration rather than the space, and under that scoping it is true and the corpus behaves correctly on either reading. If a v2 is ever authored, 'the closed enumeration of what this fixture pins' would put the scoping in the sentence rather than leaving it to the reader.
